newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura yet to confirm former president's arrest.
newsitem.headline: Nomura yet to confirm former president's arrest.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Friday it could not confirm the reported arrest of its former president Hideo Sakamaki in connection with a scandal involving allegedly illegal payoffs to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer.
A company spokeswoman said, however, that Nomura may hold a news conference around noon.
NHK television reported on Friday morning that Tokyo prosecutors had arrested Sakamaki.

Sakamaki, who stepped down as president in March and is now an adviser to the leading brokerage, told a parliamentary panel this week that he had briefly met the alleged corporate racketeer at the heart of the scandal, Ryuichi Koike, in 1992, but denied knowledge of any stock deals by Koike through Nomura.

Earlier this month, Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission, filed a complaint with prosecutors against Nomura, two former Nomura executives and a company official alleging they had illegally compensated a firm run by Koike's younger brother Yoshinori.
Prosecutors arrested the two former Nomura executives and the company official as well as the two Koike brothers.
Sokaiya typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to make a disturbance at yearly shareholders' meetings -- called "sokai" in Japanese.
